text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Urgent nephrology consultation within days for an acute nephritic syndrome with hypertension and a rise in creatinine: confirm the cause, decide whether a kidney biopsy is needed, and advise on fluid and blood pressure
  • Sodium below 2 g a day, fluids limited to about 1.5 liters a day while swollen, and daily morning weights, with a call if weight rises 1 kg in a day, urine output falls, or headache, vision change, or breathlessness appear
  • Furosemide each morning for edema and hypertension until he is back to his usual weight with normal blood pressure, with potassium and creatinine checked at each visit
  • Penicillin V for ten days to eradicate group A streptococcus
  • Stop ibuprofen and avoid all NSAIDs while the kidneys recover; acetaminophen for pain
  • Assessment for acute rheumatic fever against the 2015 revised Jones criteria, with an ECG and an echocardiogram at the consultation; secondary prophylaxis only if the criteria are met
  • Monitoring until recovery: creatinine and potassium at each visit, C3 at two and six to eight weeks, urinalysis and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at six weeks, six months, and a year, and blood pressure every year after; a kidney biopsy only if C3 stays low beyond eight weeks, creatinine keeps rising, nephrotic-range proteinuria persists, or the course is otherwise atypical

resource.title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care and nephrology for a 28-year-old composer and pianist with acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis: recognizing the acute nephritic syndrome (edema, cola-colored urine, hypertension, a rising creatinine, and red cell casts) two to three weeks after a sore throat; confirming a recent group A streptococcal infection and a low C3 with a normal C4; telling it apart from IgA nephropathy and IgA vasculitis, lupus, C3 glomerulopathy, and acute rheumatic fever, with the 2015 revised Jones criteria and an echocardiogram for the joint pains; outpatient supportive care with salt and fluid restriction, a loop diuretic, and blood pressure thresholds; antibiotics for the infection; avoiding NSAIDs; knowing when a kidney biopsy is needed; and following C3, creatinine, proteinuria, and hematuria until they recover. A sick visit for a cold teaches when not to test for strep, and the difference between synpharyngitic hematuria and a post-streptococcal relapse. Built on the KDIGO 2021 glomerular diseases guideline, the AHA 2015 Jones criteria statement, the IDSA 2012 streptococcal pharyngitis guideline, and the CMID chronic kidney disease and hypertension monographs.
